result.title: Some Memories Must Fade: Persistence and Decay of User Memories in Model Parameters
result.summary: Parametric memory allows Large Language Models to internalize knowledge directly into their weights, offering a potentially powerful alternative to retrieval-based memory (RAG). However, existing approaches to parametric memory are difficult to deploy as they largely mirror the Continual Learning (CL) objective of retaining information indefinitely. This is neither sustainable nor sufficient for a memory system, which must govern knowledge across its lifecycle by retaining stable facts, reinforcing recurring observations, updating changed beliefs, and allowing transient information to fade. We propose a system for parametric memory management consisting of a memory substrate (handling information storage and forgetting) and a learned policy (what to remember, how deeply, and for how long). Our substrate is a fixed-capacity LoRA adapter that consists of k-hot rank combinations which store facts without catastrophic interference and maintain an independently controlled temporal decay, enabling outdated information to fade while long-term facts persist. On this substrate, we train a lightweight controller that governs each incoming user event to ensure the memory system reflects the user's true, updated belief state. To evaluate how memory systems manage user memory, we introduce a controlled dataset of long-horizon user trajectories with varying persistence of facts based on changing belief states and user-behavioral shifts, and probe queries that test recall while information is valid and abstention after it expires. Our policy learns to effectively manage user memory over its entire lifecycle, balancing recall and abstention to achieve 86% of oracle performance, unlike CL and RAG baselines that primarily default to one of the two behaviors. By providing the first system to manage memory directly in model weights, this work establishes a foundation for long-horizon parametric memory.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建了一套参数化记忆管理系统：以固定容量、k-hot 秩组合的 LoRA 适配器作为可独立控制时间衰减的记忆基底，再训练轻量控制器决定每条用户事件是否写入、写多深、保留多久，并配套长程用户轨迹数据集，考察信息有效期内回忆、过期后弃答。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「学到的控制器决定写入深度与保留时长、过期即弃答」可供核查是否能借鉴为 LVR 中潜状态证据的持久/淘汰与停止决策机制，但当前文本侧、面向用户事实记忆，跨模态与推理期状态的联系尚需核查。
